text:
emma: quick sync — important: Solaris (enterprise pilot) wants an account-level pooled surge credit (not per-route). They want 6 bursts/month, 12h each, shared across routes. No commit increase. We need product/eng/finance/legal alignment by EOW.

hao: whoa pooled bursts are different from earlier asks. ops risk: pooling means unpredictable distribution across tenants unless we bind to account token quota. Need clear enforcement.

lucy: from sales: Solaris insists pooled model because they have many small routes and want flexibility. They also require visibility on remaining pooled hours per billing period.

omar: eng note: propose `surge_pool` object at account level: fields: `monthly_bursts`, `max_hours_each`, `max_tokens_total`, `per_route_max_percent`. Example (conceptual): `surge_pool: monthly_bursts=6, max_hours_each=12, max_tokens_total=1_000_000_000, per_route_max_percent=40`. Runtime can enforce per-route cap so single route can't burn whole pool.

financebot: finance view: pooled model complicates invoicing and attribution. We need a pilot floor and clear overage pricing. Suggest: first 3 bursts complimentary, then billed at on-demand with a monthly pilot minimum $5k. Also require 24h reporting SLA for pool consumption.

legalbot: Solaris asked for non-recalibration clause: "Pooled surge consumption during the pilot will not be used to adjust baseline commitments for 180 days post-pilot." We'll draft language but recommend explicit measurement windows.

emma: product proposed launch criteria: 1) eng spec + runtime enforcement + per-route cap, 2) pool usage telemetry + Console tile showing pool remaining and per-route contributions, 3) billing text + pilot addendum, 4) legal addendum with non-recalibration clause, 5) ops runbook with deterministic triggers and throttles.

hao: triggers: start when cluster_cpu>82% OR account_pool_utilization>75% for 4min; stop when both under 60% for 6min. Also need a per-route emergency throttle if a route hits per_route_max_percent.

lucy: Console: must show a single pooled counter and per-route breakdown. Customers want a weekly CSV export for internal chargebacks. Can we do weekly?

financebot: weekly CSV ok during pilot only. We'll keep monthly by default. Also require an audit event for each pooled-burst: `surge_pool.alloc` with fields route_id, tokens, hours_used.

omar: telemetry events yes — will emit `surge_pool.start`, `surge_pool.end`, `surge_pool.usage`. We'll also tag token attribution so finance can reconcile.

legalbot: contract language should also specify Redwood's protective measures: replace broad throttle language with deterministic triggers. Solaris is sensitive to wording, want "reasonable protective measures with explicit trigger list". We'll include trigger table in addendum.

emma: ops concern: cold starts if many routes spike concurrently. Proposal: prewarm buffer N=3 instances per dedicated pool when surge_pool enabled; cost billed to customer as part of surge consumption or separate prewarm addon?

financebot: recommend prewarm cost be included in pilot floor; for GA we should itemize prewarm as optional addon. For pilot keep it simple.

lucy: Solaris wants one onboarding test burst (2h) free to validate instrumentation. Fine?

emma: ok for goodwill. Note: don't change pilot floor.

hao: fallback policy: if pooled bursts cause sustained neighbor impact (p99 increase > 30% for >10min), then 1) throttle lowest priority pool routes, 2) if continues, auto-fallback to smaller quantized variant for low-priority traffic, 3) if still degrading, drain pool and fail spilled requests with 503 and reason POOL_EXHAUSTED. All deterministic in runbook.

lucy: Sales ask: need tidy billing phrase to present. Draft: "Pooled Surge Credit Pilot: Solaris is granted up to 6 pooled surge events per billing month, each up to 12 hours and shared across account routes up to a total of 1B tokens. First 3 events complimentary; subsequent surge consumption billed at on-demand rates. Monthly pilot minimum $5,000. Redwood may apply reasonable protective measures as defined in the pilot addendum (triggers included)."

legalbot: soften "may apply" -> "may apply reasonable protective measures as defined in the pilot addendum" and include explicit list of triggers and the remediation steps. Also include an accuracy SLA for reporting (24h) plus dispute window of 30 days for usage claims.

financebot: also require that pooled-burst tokens are excluded from commit recalibration for 180 days post-pilot. addendum should state measurement windows and methodology.

emma: acceptance criteria checklist: eng PR for `surge_pool` + runbook, telemetry + Console tile + weekly CSV for pilot, pilot addendum signed, finance floor confirmed, sim showing <12% neighbor impact at configured per_route_max_percent. Decision: Emma after sim.

hao: I'll prototype runtime enforcement and sim. Expect sim numbers by Wed. Ticket INF-10112 created.

opsbot: INF-10112 created and assigned to hao, omar, financebot  due 2026-05-21.

lucy: I'll prep sales one-pager and include sample invoice language.

legalbot: drafting addendum now; will include explicit triggers and dispute windows. Delivery Wed EOD.

emma: thanks team. if sims look good we'll sign Solaris pilot next Tue. I'll post decision memo after sims. :thumbsup:
